newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 20.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Economic growth rate of Tibet surpasses national average for the first time in history, reaching 10 percent in 1996
- Premier Li Peng meets Hong Kong Chamber of Commerce officials and says mainland prosperity and stability linked with Hong Kong
- Commentary calls for stronger ties between party and masses
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- China hopes relations with South Korea will continue to develop, Chinese Premier Li Peng tells visiting Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha

- Premier Li Peng says that after Hong Kong's return to the motherland, all commercial activities conforming to the Basic Law will develop smoothly and Chinese and foreign invested enterprises will enjoy equal treatment.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Industrial and Commercial Bank of China increases 4.0 billion yuan loans to individuals to buy houses
- Everbright sets up Shanghai offices
- Hunan Trust and Investment Corp approved to do foreign exchange business
- Three Gorges Security Co sets up Beijing office
ECONOMIC DAILY
- Hongtashan cigarette makes a pre-tax profit of 8.09 billion yuan last year, earned $115 million foreign exchange
BEIJING ECONOMIC DAILY
- By May 15, sales of tradeable bonds reached 687 million yuan, accounting for 12.04 percent of the total, far below non-tradeable bonds
CHINA DAILY
- A further relaxation in inflationary pressure in China was achieved last month, amid an accelerating growth of investment in fixed assets and brisk market demand for manufactured goods.
- The second 66-man contingent of the advance party of People's Liberation Army soldiers arrives in Hong Kong
